title: Salsiccia e fagioli
subtitle: Italian sausage and cannellini bean stew
excerpt: Salsiccia e fagioli is a Tuscan peasant stew of pork sausages and cannellini beans cooked in tomato and sage. It is one of the most comforting dishes in the Tuscan repertoire: simple, warming, and improved by a day's rest. Good-quality Italian-style sausages make all the difference.
sourceNotes: Tuscan regional recipe. Sausages braised with white beans is a staple of Florentine and broader Tuscan cooking. Method drawn from Anna Del Conte, Gastronomy of Italy (2001), and traditional Tuscan fagioli preparations.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freezes well without the sausage casings. Thaw and reheat gently.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the recipe and freeze half.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Makes ahead well. The flavour deepens overnight.

glossaryTerms.definition: Italian word for beans; in Tuscan cooking, fagioli almost always means dried or tinned cannellini beans, the creamy white bean used in ribollita, pasta e fagioli, and sausage stews.

content.text: is a Tuscan bean and sausage stew: Italian pork sausages browned in olive oil, then braised with cannellini beans, tomato, and sage in a single pot. The beans absorb the sausage fat and the tomato, becoming rich and creamy by the end of the 30-minute cook. It needs nothing alongside except crusty bread.
Brown {{sausages-pork}} of sausages in {{olive-oil}} of olive oil in a casserole over medium-high heat, turning, for 6 to 8 minutes until deep brown on most sides. Remove.

In the same pan, cook {{garlic}} of garlic for 1 minute. Add the sage and rosemary if using. Pour in {{dry-white-wine}} of wine, scraping up any bits. Add {{tinned-tomatoes}} of crushed tomatoes and {{stock-chicken}} of stock. Bring to a simmer.

Add {{cannellini-beans}} of drained beans. Return the sausages. Cover loosely and simmer for 25 minutes, stirring occasionally. Crush a few beans with the back of a spoon to thicken the sauce. Season well and serve with bread.

items.cause: Tinned beans are already cooked; they only need warming through.
items.fix: Add the beans with 15 minutes to go, not from the start.
Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes. Crushing some beans also thickens the sauce quickly.

content.text: Salsiccia e fagioli is at the core of Tuscan cucina povera: hearty, warming, made from shelf-stable ingredients, and deeply satisfying. The Tuscans are known for their devotion to white beans, eating them in salads, soups, and stews year-round. This version, with sausage and sage, is the winter form: it is made on cold evenings when the pot can sit on the hob for half an hour without anyone watching it.
